newsitem.title: GERMANY: Arson suspected in German apartment house blaze.
newsitem.headline: Arson suspected in German apartment house blaze.

text.p: A fire that gutted a four-storey apartment house in the western German city of Essen early on Monday, injuring 21 of its 60 mainly foreign residents, was probably started deliberately, a police spokesman said.
But he added that prosecutors still did not know how the fire began, and had no indications of a racist motive.
Earlier, police had ruled out any suspicion of arson after an initial investigation of the house, which they at first wrongly described as a home for asylum-seekers.
Later they said it was a tenement block where some 60 people were registered.
Most of the injured were taken to hospital suffering from smoke inhalation. Two women broke bones jumping from a second storey window.

Memories are still vivid in Germany of a wave of racist violence and arson by right-wing extremists after German unification in 1990, in which more than 30 people died, and authorities and citizens' groups are ever watchful for any new upsurge of attacks on foreigners.
